headline: High-risk default write/egress pair: n8n can ingest and act on Botpress outputs, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress can produce chatbot content, and n8n can consume workflow inputs and route them into tools or nodes. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, but n8n’s file/API surfaces and AI Agent node make it plausible that Botpress output is treated as trusted input. This is an interaction risk, not a proven exploit.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into an n8n workflow input without sanitization
IF an n8n node treats Botpress text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add an explicit sanitize/escape step before any n8n tool node
Require a human review step for Botpress-generated instructions
Prefix Botpress content as untrusted data in workflow templates
Disable automatic tool execution on free-text fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no network egress, but n8n has broad egress and reads/writes the server filesystem. If Botpress outputs sensitive user content into n8n workflows, n8n can transmit it to third-party integrations or persist it on disk. The pair’s shared data path is plausible from the profiles, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress handles sensitive user messages that are passed into n8n
IF an n8n workflow sends those fields to an external integration or writes them to disk
mitigations: Mask or redact sensitive fields before handing data to n8n
Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege integrations
Turn off persistence for sensitive workflow payloads where possible
Audit workflows for external API nodes that receive Botpress content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while n8n can execute shell commands and write the filesystem on the server. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate shared server state if co-located, and n8n’s per-execution shared state increases collision risk. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Botpress and n8n share the same host or writable directory
IF n8n Execute Command or Code nodes run against paths Botpress also uses
mitigations: Separate Botpress and n8n onto different hosts or containers
Mount distinct writable directories for each service
Disable n8n Execute Command nodes in shared environments
Add file-locking around any shared workspace paths
requires-engineering: introduce orchestration-level isolation and quotas

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate conversational outputs, and n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate downstream tools. If n8n treats Botpress output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into external actions through broad integrations. The profiles show a direct action-taking path, so the blast radius can extend beyond a single work product.
conditions: IF n8n uses Botpress output as an input to an AI Agent or integration node
IF downstream nodes act without verification on Botpress-produced claims
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action node
Require structured outputs with schema validation
Limit action nodes to read-only mode until reviewed
Log provenance for Botpress-derived fields before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent and n8n processes whatever workflow data it is given, with server-side secrets and per-integration OAuth scopes. If support data includes regulated personal data, n8n can route it into external systems with different retention or residency rules. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF customer-support data includes regulated personal data
IF an n8n workflow sends that data to an integration with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Classify support data before it enters n8n
Block regulated fields from non-compliant integrations
Document retention and residency for each workflow node
Review credential scopes for each connected system
